families.name: A. H11 Pro run-count — post-era N=10 extension overwrote the manifest operand in place
families.mechanism: Every row in this family reduces to one operand: outputs/h11/pv-diag-384/pro-high-text-n5/study_manifest.json $.runs_per_condition. That file was rewritten in place on 2026-03-29 by an N=10 --resume extension: it now carries $.study.name 'H11: 384px Pro HIGH — Text N=10', $.study.created '2026-03-29', $.generated '2026-03-29T01:09:52.043996+00:00', $.conditions ['text-t0.7'], $.runs_per_condition 10, $.total_units 5 and an $.execution_order listing only run_6..run_10 — i.e. the artefact records the EXTENSION, not the original study. Arithmetic: era 5 + 5 + 1 + 1 = 12 (the document's figure); current 10 + 5 + 1 + 1 = 17 (the recompute's 'actual' for 031#4/5/6/10/17[0]/20/21/22, abs_error 5.0 on every one). 031#3[0] is the same operand read directly ('all 5 runs within pro-high-text-n5'), era 5 vs current 10. 031#17[2] is the two-condition subtotal, era 5 + 5 = 10 vs current 10 + 5 = 15. The document was faithful at its own era on every one of these ten values; the artefact moved four days later. Under ruling 14 (era-faithful + artefact moved) this is SNAPSHOT-DIVERGENCE, and the dated filename is advisory only — it did not decide the disposition, the run timestamps did.

families.name: B. v2 audit F1 figures bound to the pairwise permutation record instead of the consensus sweep the document actually quotes
families.mechanism: The extraction anchored the whole of claims 12 and 13 to the pairwise permutation records (condition_a.global_f1 = 0.8404 text / 0.6998 image), and the recompute duly reported those as 'actual'. But the document's quoted figures come from the per-condition consensus sweeps, and they match those to the digit: Pro HIGH text pool 5 / threshold 3 F1 = 0.8489 -> the document's 0.849 (031#12[0]); Pro HIGH image pool 5 / threshold 3 F1 = 0.7031 -> the document's 0.703 (031#13[0]). Both sweeps carry metadata.buffer_metres = 20, so the 'F1 at 20 m' framing is satisfied. Neither artefact moved — the pairwise records and the consensus reports are byte-identical at the era commit and today (only their directory moved, results/ -> archive/results-60-tile-validation/, in 276e4ca80, 2026-04-16). So this is neither divergence nor a document defect: the extractor picked the wrong artefact for these two values. Re-anchoring makes both rows MATCH. Note the extraction's own anchor note on claim 12 flagged the possibility ('a Flash HIGH text 3-of-5 F1 may instead live in the sibling ... consensus-analysis-report.json ... Triage should choose between the two'); the sibling is indeed the right source, for value 0 as well as for the Flash value (see family C).

families.name: C. v2 audit misattributes the Pro arm's own pairwise F1 to Flash
families.mechanism: reports/configuration-audit-2026-03-25-v2.md:313-315 reads: 'Pro HIGH text consensus F1=0.849 (3-of-5 threshold) is a real Pro result ... close to but not clearly better than Flash HIGH text (F1=0.840 at 3-of-5 from the same comparison).' No era artefact supports 'Flash HIGH text F1=0.840 at 3-of-5' at 20 m. The cited pairwise record's Flash arm is labelled 'Flash HIGH text 5-of-5' with global_f1 0.7788, and the Flash HIGH text consensus sweep gives 3-of-5 = 0.6034 and 5-of-5 = 0.7761. I swept every consensus-analysis-report.json in the era tree for an f1 beginning 0.84: the only 20 m hit is the PRO text sweep's own 0.8489; the remaining hits are 30/40/50 m buffer-sensitivity rows (flash-high-image-50m 0.8427/0.8458, pro-high-image-40m 0.8477, pro-high-text-30m 0.8452/0.8474). The maximum era F1 for any Flash text condition at 20 m is 0.8136 (flash-high-text-n30, pool 30 threshold 26). 0.840 is instead the rounded value of condition_a.global_f1 = 0.8404 — the PRO arm of the very comparison the sentence cites. Both the number and the '3-of-5' label attached to it are therefore wrong at the document's own era; the sentence restates the Pro figure as if it were the Flash comparator. This is a mechanism (b) defect-at-era, not divergence: the artefact has not changed since the era commit. Corroboration that 0.840 belongs to Pro elsewhere in the project: docs/notes/working-notes.md:4963 ('Pro HIGH text N=5: F1=0.840'), :5719 (table row 'Consensus N=5 (Pro HIGH) | 0.840'), :6163 ('Pro H text 3/5 consensus: $54.06 for F1=0.840').

families.name: D. v1 audit 'T (range)' column sourced from the prompt-config default as it stood at audit time, not from the executed run metadata
families.mechanism: Five inventory-table cells report a temperature that contradicts every run meta in the phase, in both directions — phase1-library document 0.0 / executed 1.0; phase2d, phase2e, retest/phase2d, retest/phase2e document 1.0 / executed 0.0. The common cause is that the column reproduces the prompt-config JSON's temperature as it stood on 2026-03-25, not the temperature the runs actually used. At the era commit, prompts/configs/library_pure-positive-canon.json = 0.0, detect_brief-text-image_terse.json = 1.0 and detect_brief-text-image.json = 1.0 — exactly the five documented cells. Two independent drift paths made those config values wrong for the runs: (i) phase1-library executed 2026-02-01, when library_pure-positive-canon.json still read temperature 1.0 (commit d06eacd0e, 2026-02-01); the config was edited to 0.0 a week later (953e2d26d, 2026-02-08), so the March audit read a post-execution value; (ii) phase2d/phase2e (and their retests) ran under a study-level override — studies/phase2d-h5-negtext.yaml:50 'optimal_temperature: 0.0' and :76 'temperature: 0.0', studies/phase2e-h4-ordering.yaml:31 'optimal_temperature: 0.0' — which the runner DID propagate into the metadata (0.0), while the config file kept its 1.0 default. Either way, at the document's own era the run metadata already recorded the executed value, and the document contradicts it. Not divergence: these metas are dated February/mid-March 2026 and are unchanged. Control that isolates the defect to these rows: the same column is correct for the phases where config default and executed value coincide — phase2a 50/50 metas at 1.0 (document 1.0), phase2b 20 each at 0.0/0.3/0.7/1.0/1.3 (document '0.0-1.3'), phase2c 80/80 at 0.0 (document 0.0).

families.name: E. phase2d census — carried-forward conditions are tracked symlinks the manifest locator cannot see
families.mechanism: The document's row 'phase2d (neg-text) | 6 | 60' is a directory census and is correct both at era and today. Each of the two phase2d tracks holds THREE condition directories — minimal, terse, verbose — with ten run directories each: 2 x 3 x 10 = 6 conditions, 60 runs. The 'minimal' condition is a carried-forward baseline realised as symlinks (track1-image/minimal/run_N -> ../../../phase2c/track1-image/plus-hp/run_N; track2-text/minimal/run_N -> ../../../phase2b/track2-text/T0.0/run_N), and those symlinks are themselves git-tracked, so the 6/60 census is verifiable from the tracked tree. The extraction instead computed the planned product from the two study manifests, whose $.conditions lists only ['terse','verbose'] (the executed-natively subset) with runs_per_condition 10: (2+2) = 4 conditions and (2+2) x 10 = 40 runs — the recompute's 'actual' values. The manifests are era-stable; nothing moved. This is a locator failure: len:$.conditions and conditions x runs_per_condition systematically miss carried-forward/symlinked conditions. Re-anchoring to a directory census (following symlinks) makes all three rows MATCH. Cross-check that the census reading is the document's convention: the sibling phase2e row '4 | 40' is likewise a census in which one of the four conditions (config-default) is a symlinked carry-forward of phase2c plus-hp, and that row matched.

families.name: G. retest/phase3c track1-image — six in-flight batch runs landed hours after the audit

Reconstructing the era population from execution timestamps: exactly 119 of the 125 runs had started before 2026-03-25T02:30Z, and the remaining six started at 03:23:55Z, 04:09:12Z, 04:38:57Z, 05:08:16Z, 05:51:52Z and 06:38:32Z on 2026-03-25 — i.e. after the audit ran, on the same day. The document was faithful at its era; the artefact population grew within hours. Ruling 14: era-faithful + artefact moved => SNAPSHOT-DIVERGENCE. SECONDARY MECHANISM, recorded so the ledger is not misled: the extraction's expression is the PLANNED product (25 conditions x runs_per_condition 5 = 125), which equalled 125 at era too — so a naive era re-run of this expression would NOT have exonerated the document. The correct locator for this cell is an executed-run census; under that locator the row is era-MATCH and current-MISMATCH, which is the honest divergence reading. Both mechanisms are live here and the repairs differ (rider vs re-anchor), so both are recorded.

row_level_exceptions.note: Sits in a claim whose other four values belong to family B/its sibling; adjudicated separately as family C because its mechanism is a document misattribution, not an anchor choice. Within claim 13 the same split appears benignly: 13[0] (0.703) comes from the consensus sweep while 13[3] (0.727 Flash image) and 13[4] (p=0.018) come from the pairwise record and matched — so the document mixes two sources inside a single sentence. That mixing is what made a single claim-level anchor unsafe.

Dual mechanism. Primary disposition SNAPSHOT-DIVERGENCE (era population 119, verified by timestamps; grew to 125 the same day). Secondary EXTRACTION issue: the bound expression is a planned product (25 x 5) that equals 125 at era as well, so era re-resolution of the CURRENT expression would not have shown the document faithful. Any ledger row should carry both, or the divergence will look unverifiable when the era_check lands.

The document's 6/60 census is right, but note in passing (not one of my rows) that the same audit's 'Has meta.json 1,740/1,740' and 'Phase 1-2 original 335 runs' totals count 30 run directories whose payload is symlinked (20 phase2d minimal, 10 phase2e config-default) as if they were native meta-bearing runs. That is defensible at era — the symlinks resolved — but a present-day recount of native metas gives 305, not 335. Flagged for whoever adjudicates the grand-total rows; I did not adjudicate them.

recommendations.style: append-only rider (ruling 1: snapshot-class report; body untouched)
recommendations.content: Dated rider covering two items. (1) Era scope of the '12 Pro runs' figure: correct as at 2026-03-25; the pro-high-text-n5 pool was extended to N=10 on 2026-03-29 (runs 6-10, study_manifest.json rewritten in place), so a present-day recount from the manifests gives 17 and a directory census gives 21 (the two Pro MEDIUM baselines each gained runs 2-3 on 2026-06-03). (2) Correction to 'Scientific Implications' item 2, lines 313-315: the Flash comparator quoted as 'F1=0.840 at 3-of-5 from the same comparison' is neither Flash nor 3-of-5 — the cited pairwise record's Flash arm is Flash HIGH text 5-of-5 at global_f1 0.7788, and Flash HIGH text at 3-of-5 is 0.6034; 0.840 is the rounded Pro arm value 0.8404 from that same record. The sentence's qualitative conclusion is unaffected (the paired permutation gives p=0.874 on a per-tile mean difference of 0.001772), but the quoted comparator must not be cited as a Flash figure.

Dated rider covering two items. (1) The 'T (range)' column in the Phase 1-2 Original Runs and Retest tables reproduces the prompt-config JSON default as it stood on 2026-03-25, not the temperature recorded in the run metadata. Affected rows and executed values: phase1-library 1.0 (documented 0.0), phase2d 0.0 (documented 1.0), phase2e 0.0 (documented 1.0), retest/phase2d 0.0 (documented 1.0), retest/phase2e 0.0 (documented 1.0). Cause: library_pure-positive-canon.json was edited 1.0 -> 0.0 on 2026-02-08 (953e2d26d), after phase1-library ran on 2026-02-01; and phase2d/2e ran under a study-YAML temperature override of 0.0 that the config file does not carry. Rows for phase2a, phase2b and phase2c are unaffected and verified correct. (2) The retest/phase2d Conditions cell should read 4 (track1-image and track2-text, terse and verbose each), not 2; the Runs cell (4) is correct.

Four locator lessons from these 25 rows. (a) Do not anchor run-population claims to study_manifest.json $.runs_per_condition: it is a PLAN field, overwritten in place by --resume extensions (family A, 5 -> 10 on 2026-03-29) and left stale by out-of-study additions (the Pro MEDIUM baselines, still 1 after gaining runs 2-3). Prefer a run-directory census keyed on per-run execution timestamps, which are immutable and give era resolution for free even where the tree was gitignored at era. (b) Condition and run censuses must follow symlinks: len:$.conditions missed the two carried-forward 'minimal' conditions in phase2d (family E), and the same construction would misread phase2e.
